dedupe_keys.name: esa re entry predictions esa re entry front end

description: ESA's re-entry predictions site publishes predicted re-entry windows and notices for large uncontrolled and assisted re-entries of satellites and rocket bodies, with context articles and statistics on objects that have come back since the start of the space age. The European Space Agency's Space Debris Office at ESOC in Darmstadt runs it; the Re-entry Front-end was pre-released to a limited community in November 2016 and opened to the public in April 2017. Recent notices cover Cosmos-482 (May 2025), Cluster (September 2024), ERS-2 (February 2024), Aeolus and the Long March 5B core stage, and the site explains that predictions depend on long, mid and short-term orbit propagation with gravity, drag and solar activity forecasts. Coverage is global. Format and access: public web pages with prediction notices and charts; no download format was seen. Licence: not stated on the page read; free. Caveats: predictions carry wide time windows until the last hours, and only notable objects get notices. It supports hazard exposure and emergency planning for falling debris over populated areas and airspace. Related catalogue records are the CONAE space object re-entry reports and the ESA DRAMA debris mitigation suite.
